For excellent reduced local R, primary gauge a and X=V_a retaining EVERY support, define A_0=R and A_m={g:v(g)+mf(v)>=0 for every v in X}, for finite continuous signed f. Ultrametricity proves idealness, a sufficiently large power of a lies in A_m, and A_m A_n is contained in A_(m+n). Negative f somewhere excludes every unit, so A_m is proper primary; otherwise A_m=R. A monic integral-dependence equation proves integral closedness by the uniquely least-valued leading-term contradiction whenever v(g) violates the defining bound. Infinite g-values already satisfy it. The continuous profile h_m=-v(A_m)/m lies below f. Its ACTUAL primary blowup carries effective Cartier E_(A_m), with -E_(A_m)/m relatively ample and of positive degree on EVERY contracted integral curve. Positivity therefore precedes limit identification.

The raw supremum p(f) over geometric D minorants equals the supremum over C, over rational primary/unit profiles, and sup_m h_m. G331 gives uniform rational approximation in C; a small negative rational gauge correction keeps the approximation below f and becomes ideal multiplication after common denominators. A rational competitor -v(I)/r gives I subset A_r. For an actual decreasing C-net g_i with inf g_i<=f, the directed open sets {g_i<f+epsilon} cover compact X. Put M_1=||v(A_1)|| and H_N=max_(r<=N) h_r. Writing m=kr+s, 0<=s<r, the graded inclusion gives h_m>=(kr/m)h_r-sM_1/m>=h_r-rM_1/m. Consequently H_N-NM_1/m<=h_m<=p. Every canonical degree converges pointwise to finite lower semicontinuous p. Compact increasing strict-test covers show that p is continuous exactly when H_N converges uniformly, equivalently when h_m converges uniformly. Then p belongs to geometric C and is the greatest C/D minorant. Negative gauge shifts give ||p(f)-p(F)||<=||f-F||. Finite homogeneous generation implies a continuous rational-primary envelope: generators g_j of degrees d_j give inf_m v(A_m)/m=min_j v(g_j)/d_j, by evaluating homogeneous monomials and pure powers. With L divisible by their degrees, p=-v(J)/L for J=(g_j^(L/d_j)). If f is negative somewhere, these generators are nonunits; at every nonmaximal prime some generator is a unit because A_m is unit there. Thus J is proper primary. This forward implication supplies neither general finite generation nor a universal rate.

Primary change b is exact: d(v)=v(b), T(v)=v/d(v), f_b(Tv)=f_a(v)/d(v). All defining inequalities divide by the same bounded positive d, so canonical ideals are unchanged and profiles/envelopes divide by d. For EVERY excellent normal local DOMAIN of dimension TWO, dominate a finite primary-ideal list including a by its product blowup and finite normalization. This normal projective surface is regular off the marked fibre, has finitely many singular points and normal singular local completions. These verify EXACTLY Stacks54.14.5 condition(4). This Y is an ACTUAL primary blowup: choose finite affine nonvanishing section charts of powers of O(-E), equalize degrees, and choose finite algebra generators on each chart. Section localization28.27.11 writes them as t/s_i^k. In one higher degree use s_i^K and t s_i^(K-k); their projective ratios contain every affine generator, giving an immersion and hence a closed immersion by properness. Write exceptional curves E_i, gauge E_a=sum a_i E_i with a_i>0, signed model D=sum d_i E_i, and Q_ij=deg_(E_i) O(E_j), including residue degrees. Regular local factoriality makes E_i actual effective Cartier. Off-diagonal entries are nonnegative and symmetric by effective local intersection lengths. Every contracted integral curve is one of the E_i. Feasible vectors z<=min(d,0), Qz>=0 contain -M a for large M because the negative gauge bundle is generated. Coordinate maxima preserve feasibility: keep an input's diagonal coordinate and increase its nonnegative off-diagonal terms. In the compact box above the barrier, maximize each coordinate and take the finite coordinate maximum of its maximizers. This yields the greatest z*, dominating all feasible vectors after adjoining the barrier. Z*=sum z_i* E_i is actual negative effective REAL Cartier and curve-nef on ACTUAL Y.

For any primary competitor -v(I)/s<=f_D, its divisorial part F_I has the ideal generators as sections of O(-F_I), by normal height-one intersection. At the generic point of EACH exceptional CURVE some section is nonzero after removing F_I, so its degree there is nonnegative. Thus -F_I/s is feasible and <=Z*. For every support p, use the valuation ring of Frac(R/p) and its proper centre on Y; its generic centre is off the exceptional fibre. Pull the exceptional invertible lattice with its generic trivialization to this ring. Regular generator ratios prove -v(I)/s<=f_(-F_I/s)<=f_(Z*), including killed generators. Hence p(f_D)=f_(Z*). Signed primary difference functions form a separating lattice: min(vI-vJ,vK-vH)=v(IH+KJ)-v(JH), constants come from a, and (g)+a^N separates all supports. The BFJ application is ONLY a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, dimension>=2; DVR and empty cases are direct. For a signed model F fixed by a retraction, add a negative constant barrier to the max-directed nef coefficients below F. Their bounded coordinate supremum is weak-nef. BFJ3.11 supplies substantive CLOSED-simplex continuity, and ALL-retraction infima define H on all semivaluations. Canonical ideals equal L-infinity(mW); truncation by (g)+mhat^N, N>=m max(0,-min F), extends the divisorial tests to all supports, and G331 contracts primary ideals exactly. If W is nonzero,3.14 makes H strictly negative; fixed-complex thinness gives A_thin<=-CW. The WHOLE3.18 proof applies for real t>C. At t=m+C it yields (1+C/m)W<=W_m<=W, hence 0<=H-h_m<=C max(0,-min F)/m on every support. Uniform model density and Lipschitz prove smooth CE at these exact hypotheses. If the FULL reduced conductor-quotient boundary map is injective, G331's finite singleton fibres and infinite quotient fibres make normalization restriction a homeomorphism. For H=<2,3>, b=z_1+t, A=w((b,t^2,z_2,...)), the actual downstairs primary ideals K_m=(b^m(z_1-mt),t^2b^m,t^(2m+2))+(z_2,...)^m have no t-linear term in their first generator in any characteristic. Put s=w(t),u=w(z_1),B=w(b),U=min_(j>=2)w(z_j), with U=infinity when absent. Normalize min(2s,u,U)=1; A=min(B,2s,U). All generator values are>=mA. If U=A equality holds. Otherwise A<U: when2s<=B, cancellation forces s=u=1 and the last generator gives mA+2; when B<2s and s<=u, s<=1 and the second gives mA+2s; when s>u, including infinity, B=w(z_1-mt)=u=1 and the first gives mA+1, even if m=0 in k. Thus 0<=v(K_m)/m-A<=2/m on ALL supports. Actual ample negative effective primary divisors put -A in geometric C, and K_m subset A_m gives the every-degree canonical bound.

In characteristic zero, w_infinity kills t and extra z_j and gives z_1=1; w_star kills extra z_j and has (t,b) weights(1,2). A takes values1,2. A primary generator attaining e=w_infinity(I) has a unit denominator, nonzero z_1^e coefficient and no t-linear term. Its degree-e part cannot be a scalar b^e. After z_1=b-t some t^(e-j)b^j, j<e, survives with weight<=2e-1; other total degrees cannot cancel it. Therefore w_star(I)<2w_infinity(I), and every nonzero finite positive REAL primary combination retains this strict inequality. Thus -A is outside the entire finite raw ideal cone and its canonical algebra is not finitely generated. This is CE without FG, not failure.

The retained threefold obstruction is exact: blow up the regular origin and the two rational exceptional points P,Q. For I=(z)+m^2, the x-chart is x(w,x), giving divisorial part E1+2E2+2E3. On E1=Bl_(P,Q)P^2 its negative restricts to H-eP-eQ; the joining line has degree1-1-1=-1, while the other exceptional planes have degree1. notes.summary: A signed primary-model obstacle on the normal-crossing surface has no greatest geometric C or D minorant.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves the proposed obstruction on every support over every field, using G331's entire geometric comparison. Computes a stronger signed model obstacle, exact canonical ideals, pointwise convergence with uniform error1/2 in every degree, non-FG, gauge covariance and an open family of failures. Both normal components retain CE.
notes.text:
The proposal is valid for the ACTUAL G331 geometric C/D cone over EVERY field k. Let R=k[x,y,z]_(x,y,z)/(xy), m=(x,y,z), X=V_m with ALL supports. Its finite normalization is k[x,z]_(x,z) times k[y,z]_(y,z). R is their fibre product over k[z]_(z): pairs have the same residue, and separating their two remainders reconstructs R. Component idempotents make the normalization finite and show that the conductor is exactly(x,y). The reduced quotient boundary has two source points over one target point o, with support(x,y), v_o(z)=1. G331 gives singleton fibres everywhere else.

On branch1 set f1=-1/2. On branch2 set f2=-1/2-1/(2w(y)), with 1/infinity=0. Since min(w(y),w(z))=1, w(y)>=1. Extended evaluation and reciprocal on[1,infinity] are continuous; f2 lies in[-1,-1/2]. The source functions agree at EVERY conductor fibre. The compact quotient therefore gives an actual finite continuous signed obstacle f downstairs.

Let v1 be the GENERIC branch2 monomial valuation y=z=1, killing x. For ANY proper primary ideal I, e=v_o(I) is a positive finite integer. An element attaining e has a unit denominator and a branch2 numerator with nonzero z^e coefficient in its y=0 residue. Generic monomial evaluation cannot cancel distinct monomials, so v1(I)<=e. Units give equality0. Hence every finite REAL negative primary combination obeys q(o)<=q(v1). G331's proved uniform comparison extends this to ENTIRE geometric C, including real Cartier core evaluations; taking infima in ACTUAL decreasing C-nets extends it to ENTIRE D, including bottom. Thus every geometric minorant g<=f has g(o)<=-1. Every normalized valuation on the regular second branch dominates ordinary m-order. Applying the same comparison and decreasing-limit argument gives g(w)<=g(v1)<=-1 on ALL of branch2, including arbitrary supports.

For n>=1 take the genuine primary ideal I_n=m^(2n)+x^2m^n and h_n=-v(I_n)/(2n). Ideal sum/product identities hold on EVERY support. On branch1 h_n=max(-1,-1/2-v(x)/n); on branch2 and o it is-1. ACTUAL Bl_(I_n) carries effective Cartier E_n, and -E_n/(2n) is negative effective REAL Cartier, relatively ample, and of positive degree on EVERY contracted integral curve BEFORE taking limits. Thus h_n is a geometric-core minorant of f. At every finite-x branch1 point h_n increases to-1/2. The sole branch1 point killing x is o. The constant-1 is also a competitor. Consequently the COMPLETE raw C/D supremum is p=-1/2 on branch1 minus o, and p=-1 on branch2 including o. The upper bounds hold for every geometric competitor; the lower bounds are actual positive primary competitors. This determines the entire boundary.

Generic monomial w_r(x)=r,w_r(z)=1,w_r(y)=infinity, r>=1, converges to o on EVERY element of R: polynomial minima tend to the order of the x=0 residue, or infinity when that residue is0; all local unit denominators have value0. But p(w_r)=-1/2 and p(o)=-1. Thus p is not USC or continuous. Every D function is USC as an infimum of continuous functions. A greatest C or D minorant would equal its raw supremum, so neither exists. Equivalently a greatest minorant must dominate all h_n, equal-1/2 on finite-x points, and be<=-1 at o, contradicting USC. The USC regularization p* has p*(o)=-1/2 and p*(v1)=-1. It violates the proved geometric inequality. Although p*<=f, it cannot be declared positive.

There is a stronger finite signed PRIMARY-MODEL obstacle with exactly the same failure: J=(y)+m^2 and F=(1/2)v(J)-(3/2)v(m). On branch1 F=-1/2; on branch2 F=(1/2)min(w(y),2)-3/2, in[-1,-1/2]. F(o)=-1/2 and F(v1)=-1. It is a signed actual exceptional REAL Cartier evaluation on a common primary blowup of m and J. The same h_n are below F, and the same universal inequalities give the same raw p and no greatest C/D minorant.

For BOTH obstacles, in EVERY degree m>=1 the canonical ideal is A_m=(z^m)+x(x,z)^(ceil(m/2)-1)+y(y,z)^(m-1). On branch1 the defining condition is exactly ordinary order>=ceil(m/2), by the generic order valuation and domination by all normalized supports. On branch2 it is exactly order>=m: necessity is v1, sufficiency uses f2,F2>=-1. The common z-residue of the two component functions must then have order>=m. Separating it from the x- and y-divisible remainders proves the displayed downstairs ideal identity, including local-unit denominators. If s=v(x),t=v(z), min(s,t)=1 on branch1, its canonical profile is h_m=-min(mt,s+ceil(m/2)-1)/m. On branch2 and o it is-1.

Every h_m has an ACTUAL negative effective ample primary presentation and converges pointwise in EVERY degree to p. Nevertheless ||p-h_m||=1/2 for EVERY m: take t=1 and finite s>=m-ceil(m/2)+1 to obtain h_m=-1,p=-1/2; everywhere the difference is in[0,1/2]. The canonical algebra is not finitely generated by n1's forward implication from finite generation to a continuous rational-primary envelope. Here non-FG accompanies an independently proved failure; it does not replace the regularity argument.

The failure is stable: if ||f'-f||<epsilon<1/4, h_n-epsilon are C minorants of f'. A greatest C/D minorant would be>=-1/2-epsilon along the finite-x locus, but at o the universal inequality gives value<=-1+epsilon. USC along w_r makes these incompatible.

On the unnormalized cone, lambda=v(m), the proposed second-component obstacle is-lambda/2-lambda^2/(2v(y)), with the second summand0 at infinity; the first is-lambda/2. These are degree-one homogeneous. F is already homogeneous. Raw p is-lambda/2 on finite-x first-component points and-lambda otherwise. Exact primary transport divides by the same bounded positive denominator, preserving discontinuity and nonexistence; canonical ideals are unchanged. Completion preserves the example.

This is a genuinely NONNORMAL obstruction with nonsingleton infinite-conductor fibres. Each normal surface component has CE by n1. It contradicts neither bijective normalization transport nor reduced-curve min(f,0), where conductor fibres are singletons. Literal radial extension, products, energy and full operators remain separate. Artifacts: n2.md, n2.tex, diagnostics.py and reports/diagnostics.json. Rerun: python diagnostics.py; python deliver.py; python check_delivery.py. Finite checks are observations; the argument above covers all supports.

notes.summary: Positive-dimensional intersections of distinct irreducible components obstruct geometric envelopes in every characteristic.
notes.detailedSummary: Actual conductor separators and G331's normal divisorial bound produce a strictly negative continuous signed primary-model obstacle with no greatest C/D minorant. All-support divisorial density proves the USC contradiction. The theorem needs a cross-component normalization fibre; it assumes neither source CE nor higher-dimensional resolution.
notes.text:
Let R be any excellent reduced positive-dimensional local ring, a a primary gauge, S its finite normalization, rho its FULL boundary quotient and c its conductor. Suppose one rho-fibre has lifts alpha,beta on normal centres belonging to DIFFERENT minimal components. Then a bounded strictly negative continuous SIGNED PRIMARY-MODEL obstacle on R has neither a greatest geometric C nor a greatest geometric D minorant.

Choose a regular conductor element c0. Normalization idempotents e1,e2 for the distinct domain factors give actual downstairs elements j=c0e1 and ell=c0e2, since c is an S-ideal. They vanish on all other components and are nonzero on their own. The nontrivial fibre is conductor-infinite by G331, so alpha,beta kill c0.

Choose a centred divisorial valuation nu on the normal local centre containing beta, normalized by aS. G331's normal-domain bound gives finite K>=1 with nu(I)<=K beta(I) for every primary/unit ideal there. Specifically nu(h)<=C ord_m(h) for nonunits and beta(m)>=1/r when m^r subset aS give this inequality; units are handled separately. Negative finite REAL combinations satisfy u(nu)>=K u(beta). Uniform comparison and ACTUAL decreasing infima extend it to ENTIRE geometric C and D. Pullback of a target g thus gives g(rho(beta))<=g(rho(nu))/K. This uses the normal-centre theorem, not analytic irreducibility of nonnormal R.

Let d=nu(ell)=nu(c0)>0. Choose integers L>d and B>0 with 1+B(1-d/L)>K. Set b=B+1, I=(ell)+a^L and F=(B/L)v(I)-(B+1)v(a). I is actual proper primary: ell vanishes on another component and cannot be a unit. On V_a, F is continuous in[-b,-1], equals-1 on component1 and at the common fibre, and at rho(nu) is-1-B(1-d/L)<-K. It is a signed REAL Cartier evaluation on a common primary blowup. Therefore EVERY geometric minorant g<=F has g(rho(beta))<=F(rho(nu))/K<-1.

For every n put T_n=a^(bn)+(j)a^n and q_n=-v(T_n)/n. These are actual proper primary ideals, whose negative effective REAL Cartier divisors on ACTUAL blowups are relatively ample and positive on EVERY contracted integral curve. On component1, q_n=max(-b,-1-v(j)/n); on every other component it is-b. Thus q_n<=F on EVERY support. At every component1 point with finite j-value, sup_n q_n=-1. This locus is dense in the full component1 boundary: G331's divisorial density gives a dense set of generic-support centred divisorial valuations, where j is nonzero and has finite value. Alpha belongs to its closure, although it kills the conductor.

A greatest C/D minorant would dominate all q_n and equal-1 on that dense locus because F=-1 there. Its normalization pullback is USC. A value<-1 at alpha would have a strict sublevel neighbourhood meeting this locus, a contradiction. But alpha and beta have the same target point, where EVERY minorant is strictly below-1 by the preceding inequality. Hence neither greatest minorant exists. Dense nets suffice; no metrizability or sequence extraction is assumed.

An algebraic sufficient condition is that distinct minimal primes p1,p2 have dim R/(p1+p2)>=1. The excellent positive-dimensional reduced quotient has a nonempty centred boundary by G331. A semivaluation there factors through both R/p_i and lifts through their finite normalizations to two different minimal-domain factors over the same target point. The conductor value must be infinite by finite-stratum uniqueness. Thus EVERY positive-dimensional intersection of distinct irreducible components obstructs universal continuous envelopes, in ANY dimension, characteristic or residue field, already for a signed primary-model obstacle.

Nonsingleton fibres confined to one minimal-domain normalization are not covered. General excellent normal dimension>=3 CE is not decided. No source CE, new ideal cone, resolution, arbitrary-model cofinality, norm averaging or deleted support is used. All profiles are homogeneous and exact primary-gauge transport preserves the conclusion. Artifacts: n3.md and n3.tex. Rerun: python deliver.py; python check_delivery.py. This is a universal draft proof relative to qualified G331, not original-task closure.

notes.summary: Exact crossing-surface conductor criterion, mixed-characteristic failures and a normal-component surface classification.

notes.text:
Consider R=k[x,y,z]_(x,y,z)/(xy) over any field, or R=V[[x,y]]/(xy) for a complete DVR V, with gauges m=(x,y,z) or(x,y,pi). In the latter case splitting formal series proves the fibre product V[[x]] times_V V[[y]], normalization product V[[x]] times V[[y]], and conductor(x,y). Both normalization factors are regular excellent normal surfaces. Their two conductor-boundary points map to one o. G331 supplies the full quotient and positive C/D descent.

For ANY finite continuous signed target obstacle f, let f_i be its component restrictions and H_i their greatest continuous geometric envelopes, existing by n1's arbitrary-characteristic normal-surface theorem. Let o_i be the conductor point and a=min(H_1(o_1),H_2(o_2)). Then the ENTIRE raw C/D supremum equals H_i(w) at every component point with finite w(x_i), and equals a at o, where x_1=x,x_2=y. A greatest C/D minorant exists precisely when H_1(o_1)=H_2(o_2); then the envelope is continuous and belongs to geometric C. Otherwise it is not USC and neither greatest minorant exists.

Here is the constructive lower bound with positivity. G331's normal zero dichotomy implies H_i(o_i)=0 only when H_i is identically0. If a=0 both envelopes are0 and p=0. If a<0, put B_i=(a/H_i(o_i))H_i when H_i(o_i)<0, and B_i=constant a when H_i=0. Then B_i is geometric C, B_i<=H_i<=f_i, and B_i(o_i)=a. For n>=1 define G_(i,n)=max(B_i,H_i-w(x_i)/n), taking the second term bottom when x_i is killed. Choose integer N>=n||H_i-B_i||. On the normalized section,
G_(i,n)=max(B_i,H_i-(1/n)w((x_i)+m_i^N)).
Indeed w((x_i)+m_i^N)=min(w(x_i),N), and H_i-N/n<=B_i everywhere. The right side belongs to C by granted addition, scaling and maxima, with an ACTUAL negative effective ample primary presentation for the ideal term. Thus G_(i,n) is continuous and positive in the geometric completed sense, equals a at the conductor and lies below f_i. The compatible tuple descends WITH POSITIVITY by G331, increases to H_i at finite-x_i points and retains a at o. This proves the raw lower bound. Every target D competitor pulls back to a source D minorant, hence is<=H_i and its common conductor value is<=both H_i(o_i). This proves the upper bound on ALL supports. No fibrewise minimum is silently treated as psh.

If conductor values match, the tuple H_i descends to the greatest continuous envelope. If H_1(o_1)>a, polynomial monomial w_r(x)=r,w_r(z)=1 tends on every element to o_1. In the DVR case define w_r(sum a_jx^j)=min_j(ord_pi(a_j)+rj), w_r(pi)=1. The associated graded domain proves multiplicativity, units have value0, and the values tend to ord_pi(a_0), or infinity if a_0=0. Continuity of H_1 yields p(w_r) tending to H_1(o_1)>p(o), contradicting USC of a greatest minorant.

The same criterion holds for finite q>=2 at an EXCELLENT local fibre product of excellent regular local SURFACE rings with surjective maps to the SAME marked DVR, nonzero principal kernels(x_i), and their product as finite normalization. The gauge must extend to primary gauges on every factor; all quotient points use the same quotient gauge. Take a=min_i H_i(o_i), use the same B_i and primary truncations with (x_i)+a_i^N, and require equality of ALL conductor values. At an incompatible value, G331 divisorial density supplies a convergent NET in the finite-kernel-value locus. These assumptions hold for k[x_1,...,x_q,z]_0/(x_ix_j:i!=j) and V[[x_1,...,x_q]]/(x_ix_j:i!=j), by separated-term expansion. No higher-dimensional conductor minimum field is claimed geometric.

The explicit proposed and signed model obstacles of n2 also work on V[[x,y]]/(xy), replacing z by pi. Generic branch2 order is min_j(ord_pi(a_j)+j). A generator attaining conductor order e has a nonzero pi^e coefficient in its y=0 residue, hence generic order<=e. Every arbitrary-support normalized valuation dominates ordinary m-order. The identical comparison, actual positivity and canonical ideals prove no greatest C/D minorant, with every-degree error1/2. This is a nonnormal mixed-characteristic failure, while the mixed cusp in n1 remains a CE example.

For EVERY d>=2 and field k the obstruction extends to R_d=k[x,y,z_1,...,z_(d-1)]_0/(xy). The conductor quotient is the z-ring, retaining ALL its supports.
